details.claim: Socotra is home to over 37% of its plant species found nowhere else.
Dragon's Blood Trees thrive here, their red sap a symbol of the island's isolation.
In 2008, Socotra was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

details.extra_statement: Socotra, an island of unique beauty and mystery, sits 380 kilometres south of the Arabian Peninsula.
Its landscape is a mix of arid coastal plains and rugged mountains.
Socotra's history is as intriguing as its geography.
From ancient trade routes to modern conflicts, the island's story is complex.
